findings.message: Pushbox separation has a slot bias in an edge case. packages/simulation/src/duel/step.ts:417 breaks an x tie with `aLeft = a.x < b.x || (a.x === b.x && a.facing === 1)`. When both fighters share an x and face the same way (possible after a cross-up, because only a free fighter turns), slot 0 is always pushed left. In the mirrored duel, the mirror of slot 0 is also pushed left instead of right, so the outcome depends on which slot a player has. The symmetry test's scripted exchange never reaches this state. A slot-neutral tie-break (for example, one based on each fighter's own facing or a previous-frame order kept in state) would close it.
findings.requirement: the outcome never depends on which player is first

findings.message: A guard break sets stamina to 30 (step.ts:289, `stamina: Math.min(rules.maxStamina, rules.guardBreakStaminaRestore)`) instead of adding 30. A break only happens below the block cost (at most 24 stamina), so this gives 30 where an additive reading gives 30 to 54. docs/duel.md and the worker's open assumptions state this reading, so it is not hidden, but it is a balance-relevant interpretation of the spec's wording and the operator should confirm it.
findings.requirement: a guard break staggers 30 frames and restores 30 stamina

findings.message: restoreDuel (packages/simulation/src/duel/snapshot.ts:16-26) checks only movesetVersion, a non-negative integer frame and a two-element fighters array before copying. A snapshot with a missing or malformed fighter field (for example no `buffer`, or an unknown `action` or `phase`) is accepted and fails later inside stepDuel (a TypeError on `fighter.buffer[button]`) or silently diverges. It is the documented entry point for wire checkpoints, so validating the full state shape at restore (for example with a zod schema) would make bad checkpoints fail where they enter.

The moveset validator's 'no free opening hit' check (packages/content/src/moves/schema.ts:923-927) compares startGap only with the static hitbox reach plus the hurtbox reach. It ignores a move's `advance` (the advancing thrust moves 64 sub-pixels a frame through startup and active frames). Current data passes: the thrust reaches about 2400 sub-pixels against a start gap of 3072, and a test confirms that nothing connects from the start positions. A future data change could still start fighters within reach without the validator noticing.
findings.requirement: A zod validator rejects impossible data

findings.message: packages/simulation/src/duel/duel.test.ts:327 'decides a guard break from the stamina held at the start of the frame' only probes the cost threshold (stamina 25 vs 24 against a heavy). Both runs start from createDuelState with staminaIdle 0, so the block on frame 19 happens long before the 60-frame regeneration delay. Stamina therefore has only one possible value during that frame. The test would still pass if step.ts applied regeneration (step 6) before the block cost (step 4), or read stamina after any other in-frame change. No test sets up a contact frame on which a regeneration tick lands, for example stamina 24 with staminaIdle chosen so that the tick falls on the block frame, and asserts that the guard still breaks. The implementation reads start-of-frame stamina (react() uses fighter.stamina before the regeneration pass), but no test checks this ordering.
findings.requirement: Stamina costs and guard breaks of the frame are computed from start-of-frame stamina.

findings.message: The postbuild self-checks in packages/simulation/package.json and packages/content/package.json ran and passed on the candidate (build log: both subpaths load from dist/). Only their success path has run. No test or captured evidence shows either script failing when the subpath resolves outside dist/ or the module exports nothing. The worker's claim that the script exits 1 under the source condition is not in any verification packet. The failure logic is a short inline script that can be checked by reading it, so the risk is low.
findings.requirement: each of the two packages gets a `postbuild` script that imports its new subpath from `dist/` without the source condition and fails when it resolves elsewhere or exports nothing
